mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 7 Series 730i engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 7 Series 730i engine replacement cost depends on the generation and engine code. M54B30 and N52B30 replacements typically range from £800-£1,800 for used units, £2,000-£3,800 for reconditioned, and £3,200-£5,500 for rebuilt with warranty. B48B20 replacements for G11 models cost £1,500-£2,800 used, £3,000-£5,000 reconditioned, and £4,200-£6,500 rebuilt.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of valve stem seal failure in a BMW 7 Series 730i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common symptom is blue or white smoke from the exhaust on cold startup, clearing after a few seconds. As the seals worsen, you may notice increased oil consumption between services, a slight misfire on startup, and eventually the engine warning light may illuminate.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 7 Series 730i?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - if your BMW 7 Series 730i is otherwise in good condition, a rebuilt engine from £3,200-£5,500 is often worthwhile. With 730i values ranging from £3,000-£30,000 depending on generation, replacement cost typically represents a reasonable proportion of the vehicle's value.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 7 Series 730i engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most BMW 7 Series 730i engine replacements take 1-3 days for supply and fit at a specialist garage. The complexity varies by generation - older M30 and M60 engines are simpler, while modern B48 turbo engines require more precise calibration.

mainEntity.name: Do BMW 7 Series 730i replacement engines come with a warranty?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - every rebuilt BMW 7 Series 730i engine supplied through EnginesMarket comes with a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. Used engines typically have 3-6 month warranties, while reconditioned units often include 6-12 months of cover.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the BMW 730i and 740i engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The BMW 730i has always been the entry-level petrol 7 Series, while the 740i sits above it with a larger, more powerful engine. In the G11 generation, the 730i uses a 2.0-litre turbo four-cylinder (B48B20, 258hp), while the 740i uses a 3.0-litre turbo straight-six (B58B30, 326hp). In earlier generations, the gap was smaller - the E38 730i used a 3.0-litre V8 (M60B30, 218hp) while the 740i used a 4.0-litre V8 (M60B40, 286hp).

commonProblems.h2: BMW 7 Series 730i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 7 Series 730i has worn many engine codes over its long production life, each with its own character and weak points. The most common problems driving 730i replacement searches are N52 valve stem seal failure on 2005-2015 models, M54 VANOS and DISA issues on early E65 cars, and cooling system failures across the N52 and B48 generations. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: N52 Valve Stem Seal Failure - Why the BMW 7 Series 730i N52B30 Burns Oil
problems.rootCause: The N52's valve stem seals harden and lose their sealing ability over time, allowing oil to seep past the valves and burn in the combustion chamber. This is most noticeable as blue or white smoke on cold startup.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of all 24 valve stem seals; cylinder head remains on engine
repairOptions.longevity: Cost-effective fix if caught early; resolves oil consumption

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, rebuilt N52 with upgraded seals, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If oil burning has caused catalytic converter damage or if engine is high-mileage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical BMW 7 Series 730i (E65/F01) ranges from £3,000-£12,000 depending on year and condition. For an E65 730i valued under £5,000, valve stem seal replacement at £1,500-£2,800 is often the better financial decision than a full engine replacement. For F01 730i examples valued £6,000-£12,000, a rebuilt N52 with upgraded seals can be a sound long-term investment.
problems.recommendation: If your BMW 7 Series 730i emits smoke on startup but runs smoothly otherwise, valve stem seal replacement is almost always the right call. This is a well-understood repair that specialist BMW indies perform regularly, and it costs significantly less than a full engine replacement.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt N52B30 BMW 7 Series 730i engine prices

problems.h4: M54 VANOS and DISA Failure - Rough Idle and Power Loss in the E65 730i
problems.rootCause: The M54's VANOS variable valve timing system relies on seals that harden over time, reducing oil pressure and causing timing drift. The DISA (Differentialed Intake Manifold) valve flap can also fail, breaking and potentially entering the intake manifold.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of VANOS seals; DISA valve inspection/replacement
repairOptions.longevity: Standard maintenance for M54 engines; prevents rough running

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, rebuilt M54 with updated VANOS components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If VANOS failure has caused timing chain or valve damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: With E65 730i values typically £3,000-£7,000, the VANOS repair at £500-£900 is well within the vehicle's value and strongly recommended. A full engine replacement on an E65 730i is rarely cost-effective unless the car is in exceptional condition.
problems.recommendation: M54 VANOS repair is routine maintenance for any BMW specialist. If your E65 730i has a lumpy idle or hesitation below 3,000rpm, have the VANOS seals and DISA valve checked before assuming the engine is terminally damaged.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M54B30 BMW 7 Series 730i engine prices

problems.h4: Cooling System Failures - Water Pump and Thermostat Housing Leaks (N52/B48)
problems.rootCause: BMW's electric water pumps and plastic thermostat housings are prone to failure on both N52 and B48 engines. Coolant leaks from the expansion tank, water pump and thermostat housing are common, leading to overheating if not addressed.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of electric water pump, thermostat and housing
Supply & fit, rebuilt engine with new cooling components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If overheating has caused head gasket or block damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For modern G11 730i examples valued £15,000-£30,000, water pump replacement at £500-£900 is routine maintenance. For older E65 or F01 730i examples, the repair is still well within the vehicle's value and should be prioritised to prevent catastrophic engine damage.
problems.recommendation: Cooling system failure is one of the few preventable causes of N52 and B48 engine death. If your BMW 7 Series 730i is approaching 60,000 miles, we recommend proactively replacing the water pump and thermostat - it's cheaper than a new engine.
